newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan October forex reserves up to US$87.253 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan October forex reserves up to US$87.253 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves rose to US$87.253 billion at the end of October from $86.678 billion at the end of September, the central bank said on Monday.
The bank gave no immediate explanation for the rise. Period Oct 1996 Sept 1996 Oct 1995
Note - Foreign currency reserves in billions of U.S. dollars.

Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves, the world's third largest after Japan's and China's, fell in late 1995 and early 1996 as political tensions with rival China intensified into a military crisis in March, triggering heavy capital outflows.
The trend reversed after Taiwan's March 23 presidential election and a clear easing of tensions with China. Taiwan's reserves have risen slowly but steadily since April.

Beijing, seeking to quell any moves away from Taiwan's stated goal of reunification with China, held war games and missile tests in the Taiwan strait before the presidential poll, triggering waves of U.S. dollar buying and a run on gold.
The central bank intervened during the crisis to support the Taiwan dollar and the island's hypersensitive stock market.

Taiwan's foreign reserves peaked more than one year ago at $100.412 billion in June 1995, just as tensions with China erupted over President Lee Teng-hui's controversial private visit to the United States.
